hook: The police refused to register my FIR.

slides.title: You can go to any police station.
slides.body: For a cognizable offence, the law lets you give the information at any police station, wherever the crime happened. This is called a Zero FIR.

slides.title: You can report it electronically too.
slides.body: Information can be given orally or electronically. If you report it electronically, you must sign it within 3 days.

slides.title: You get a free copy.
slides.body: Once your information is recorded, the police must give you a copy at once, free of cost.

slides.title: Still refused? Write to the SP.
slides.body: Send the details in writing, by post, to the Superintendent of Police. If it shows a cognizable offence, the SP must investigate or order an investigation.

slides.title: SP didn't act? Go to the Magistrate.
slides.body: If the SP doesn't act on it, you can apply to the Magistrate.

slides.title: One exception to know.
slides.body: For offences punishable with 3 to 7 years, police may first hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days, with a DSP's permission.

caption:
Police refused to register your FIR? Here's what the law says you can do. 👇

1️⃣ Any police station must record a cognizable offence, wherever it happened (Zero FIR)
2️⃣ You can report it electronically, then sign within 3 days
3️⃣ You get a free copy of what's recorded
4️⃣ Refused? Write to the Superintendent of Police by post
5️⃣ SP doesn't act? Apply to the Magistrate

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Section 173
